item.title: Titans LB Anthony Hill is the defensive rookie of the month
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez is the early betting favorite for defensive rookie of the year, but he wasn't the NFL's choice for defensive rookie of the month.
item.content:encoded:
Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez is the early betting favorite for defensive rookie of the year, but he wasn't the NFL's choice for defensive rookie of the month.

The NFL announced on Thursday that Titans linebacker Anthony Hill has taken that award. Hill joined the Titans as a second-round pick in April.

Hill leads the entire league with 34 tackles through the first three weeks of the regular season. He has also broken up a pair of passes so far this season.

What Hill has yet to do as a professional is win a game. The Titans are 0-3 and will take on the Ravens as they search for their first victory. If Hill can keep former Titan Derrick Henry under wraps, their chances of obtaining it will look a little better.

item.title: Vikings KR Myles Price named the NFC special teams player of the month
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Myles Price was named the NFC's special teams player of the week on Wednesday and Thursday brought another award for the Vikings wideout.
item.content:encoded:
Myles Price was named the NFC's special teams player of the week on Wednesday and Thursday brought another award for the Vikings wideout.

Price has also been named the conference's special teams player of the month. Both awards were firsts for the second-year player.

Price's biggest play in September came last Sunday when he returned a punt 86 yards for a touchdown in Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers. It was Price's first NFL touchdown and the first kick return for a touchdown of any kind in the league this year.

Price is averaging 21.4 yards per punt return and he also leads the league with 353 kickoff return yards.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Evan McPherson has been a critical piece for Cincinnati’s success through the season’s first three weeks and the league has now recognized him for it.
item.content:encoded:
Evan McPherson has been a critical piece for Cincinnati’s success through the season’s first three weeks and the league has now recognized him for it.

McPherson has been named AFC special teams player of the month for September.

McPherson was 8-of-8 on his field goal attempts, hitting five from at least 50 yards. He also connected on all eight of his extra points.

This is McPherson’s second career special teams player of the month award, making him the only Bengals player to ever win it multiple times.

After a down year in 2024, McPherson hit 89 percent of his field goals last season, with his only three misses coming from over 50 yards.

item.title: Greg Rousseau named AFC defensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Greg Rousseau has put together an impressive start to the 2026 season and the league has taken notice.
item.content:encoded:
Greg Rousseau has put together an impressive start to the 2026 season and the league has taken notice.

Rousseau has been named AFC defensive player of the month for September.

Through three weeks, Rousseau leads the league with 6.0 sacks, eight tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles.

According to the league, he is the third player since 1982 — when the sack became an official stat — with at least 2.0 sacks in each of a team’s first three games. Mark Gastineau accomplished the feat in 1984 and Kevin Greene did it in 1998.

This is Rousseau’s first career defensive player of the month award.

He also is just 2.0 sacks away from his career-high of 8.0, which he registered in 2022 and 2024.

The Bills will host the Patriots on Sunday.

item.title: Giants S Jevon Holland named the NFC defensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants wrapped up a 12-7 win over the Titans last Sunday when safety Jevon Holland intercepted a pass in the end zone and the play also wrapped up a stellar month for Holland.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants wrapped up a 12-7 win over the Titans last Sunday when safety Jevon Holland intercepted a pass in the end zone and the play also wrapped up a stellar month for Holland.

Holland had an interception in each of the three games that the Giants played in September, which has already given him a career high for a single season. Holland was also credited with 12 tackles, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery while helping the team to a 2-1 start to the year.

On Thursday, the NFL recognized Holland's effort by naming him the NFC's defensive player of the month for September.

Holland will try to add to his exploits against the Cardinals this Sunday and the Giants will take all that he can give after losing quarterback Jaxson Dart and linebacker Brian Burns to season-ending knee injuries over the last couple of weeks.

item.title: Kenneth Walker named AFC offensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 and the reigning Super Bowl MVP is a big reason why.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 and the reigning Super Bowl MVP is a big reason why.

Running back Kenneth Walker has been named AFC offensive player of the month.

Walker leads the league with 360 yards rushing through three weeks. He’s also totaled 442 yards from scrimmage with four total touchdowns — two rushing and two receiving.

Walker became the first player in league history with a rushing and receiving touchdown in two of his first three games with a team.

The league notes Walker is also the fifth player ever with at least 175 yards from scrimmage in each of his first two games with a season, joining Jim Brown (1963), O.J. Simpson (1975), Paul Hofer (1980), and Billy Sims (1980).

This is Walker’s first career player of the month award.

Walker and the Chiefs will be in Las Vegas this weekend to play the division-rival Raiders.

item.title: Brock Purdy is the NFC offensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers have dealt with a slew of injuries over the first month of the season, but quarterback Brock Purdy has stayed healthy and he's a big reason why the team is 3-0.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have dealt with a slew of injuries over the first month of the season, but quarterback Brock Purdy has stayed healthy and he's a big reason why the team is 3-0.

Purdy has gone 60-of-83 for 789 yards, nine touchdowns and an interception so far this season. His nine touchdown passes lead the league and he leads the league in a number of other metrics, including quarterback rating. On top of that, Purdy has not been sacked yet this year.

That production and the 49ers' record made Purdy the NFL's choice for the NFC offensive player of the month for September.

Purdy was also the NFC offensive player of the week in Week 2, but this is the first time that he's taken the monthly prize.

item.title: Report: Joey Porter Jr. trade has a term that protects against an ongoing hold-in
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In trading for former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., the Cowboys are taking a leap of faith that Porter will play without a new contract.
item.content:encoded:
In trading for former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., the Cowboys are taking a leap of faith that Porter will play without a new contract.

The Cowboys have some protection against the possibility of Porter not playing.

Via Todd Archer of ESPN, the 2027 sixth-round pick is tied to Porter being on the gameday roster for at least two games before that selection goes through.

While the second-round pick in 2028 isn't attached to that caveat, the Cowboys would be in line for a 2028 third-round compensatory pick if Porter leaves as a free agent in March.

If Porter immediately suits up for Sunday's game against the Texans, the term most likely will be satisfied. If, for some reason, the "back" and "conditioning" issues linger, the Cowboys will keep their 2027 sixth-round pick.

item.title: PFT's Week 4 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A quick look at all 16 games for the coming weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Maybe it's good that I'm no longer doing the Joint Mega Picks Podcast.

From 10-6 to 9-7 to 8-8, the trend is not my friend. (For the season, I'm 27-21.)

In Week 3, the best pick was Ravens over Cowboys (especially since the wild-guess score prediction was 34-30). Worst pick: Buccaneers over Vikings. Flew too close to the sun on wings of pastrami pick: Bengals over Steelers, based on the erroneous conclusion that Pittsburgh's find-a-way magic dried up when Mike Tomlin left town.

But each week brings another opportunity to land closer to 16-0 than 0-16. Hopefully, this year's weekly one-game slide won't result in 7-9.

Steelers at Browns (Thursday night)

The Steelers have gone 1-7 in Cleveland since 2018. To make matters worse, the Steelers are 0-9 in Thursday night games against AFC North rivals.

What better way to turn the page on the recent past than to go to Cleveland and find a way to win? Aaron Rodgers will need to get his 42-year-old body ready to go on a short week, and the Steelers will need to play well on both sides of the ball.

Browns coach Todd Monken has plenty of experience against the Steelers, given his time with the Ravens. My brain is screaming "Browns!" but my gut is saying that the Steelers will benefit from coach Mike McCarthy's 16-6 record in short-week games.

Steelers 17, Browns 13.

Colts vs. Commanders at London

The Colts ended a long losing streak, thanks to a Texans team that still can't find a way out of its early-season struggles. The Commanders stunned the defending Super Bowl champions, fueled by the kind of performance from Marcus Mariota that will keep Jayden Daniels on the bench until the 32-year-old former full-time starter cools off. Mariota may have at least one more in the tank.

Commanders 24, Colts 20.

Titans at Ravens

Derrick Henry faces his former team for the first time. He'll make them regret letting him go, if they don't already.

Making that task easier is that the Titans can't get anything going. Coach Robert Saleh's reference to quarterback Cam Ward's sacks-induced PTSD means that the clock in his brain is running out before the walls close in on a given play. That likely won't be cured against the Ravens' defense in Baltimore.

Ravens 30, Titans 17.

Patriots at Bills

Of all the teams in the NFL, none relish the regression of the Patriots more than the Bills. On Sunday, Buffalo could essentially nail down the AFC East and set the table for a run to the No. 1 seed, given their ability to run roughshod against overmatched division rivals.

Bills 34, Patriots 21.

Jets at Bears

Former Lions coordinators get together in Chicago. The Jets are improving, but the Bears have the better team on both sides of the ball — even without their starting quarterback. Or their preferred backup.

Bears 27, Jets 17.

Jaguars at Bengals

Trevor Lawrence has beaten every team in the AFC except the Bengals. Last year, Jake Browning engineered the win after Joe Burrow left with a toe injury. And if, as Burrow believes, the 2026 Bengals have 2019 LSU vibes, a 2-2 start is not acceptable.

Bengals 28, Jaguars 27.

Cowboys at Texans

The battle of Texas takes a back seat to the fact that both teams need this one, badly. Until Houston can muster consistent and effective offense, it's hard to envision them turning it around.

Last year, the Texans became the second team to get to the playoffs after starting 0-3. This year, they may end up having a chance to be the second team to get there after starting 0-4.

Cowboys 27, Texans 20.

Cardinals at Giants

The Giants have a chance to get another win while they further adjust to life without Jaxson Dart. And Jameis Winston needs to start worrying about staving off J.J. McCarthy.

Giants 23, Cardinals 17.

Rams at Eagles

Last year, a wild play on a game-winning field-goal attempt by the Rams gave the Eagles a win. This year, the Rams will make sure to not let it be that close.

Rams 30, Eagles 20.

Packers at Buccaneers

The Bay of Pigs is back. If Green Bay with extra time to prepare can't beat an undrafted rookie quarterback making his first start, they should dissolve the corporation.

Packers 21, Buccaneers 13.

Dolphins at Vikings

This is a candidate for Correction Sunday. But the Dolphins have lost one of their best players for the year (De'Von Achane) and the Vikings' defense is good enough to win games even if the offense adopts a punt-on-first-down strategy.

Vikings 24, Dolphins 14.

Chiefs at Raiders

The NFL is better when the Raiders are good. It's at its best when the Chiefs-Raiders rivalry is relevant.

Chiefs 23, Raiders 16.

Chargers at Seahawks

There's plenty of Harbaugh DNA in this one, literally and figuratively. That won't matter much, because the Seahawks got an unexpected wakeup call against the Commanders.

Seahawks 27, Chargers 13.

Broncos at 49ers

The Shanahan Bowl has high stakes for both teams. While the injuries are piling up (again) in San Francisco, they have enough to hold serve in the latest potential Super Bowl preview.

49ers 24, Broncos 20.

Lions at Panthers

The Panthers have carried over less of the "division champs" vibe and more of the "8-9-for-a-reason" vibe. And the Lions definitely can't afford to lose games they should win.

Lions 31, Panthers 21.

Falcons at Saints

Twenty years after one of the most significant regular-season games in New Orleans history between these two teams, the Saints can't lose to their most despised rivals, can they?

Saints 23, Falcons 17.

item.title: Jayden Daniels on return from dislocated elbow: Just taking it day by day
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returned to practice on Wednesday for the first time since dislocating his left elbow in the team's Week 2 loss to the Cowboys and he his return to game action was a chief topic at his press conference on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returned to practice on Wednesday for the first time since dislocating his left elbow in the team's Week 2 loss to the Cowboys and he his return to game action was a chief topic at his press conference on Thursday.

Daniels has not been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Colts in London and he was asked if he thinks he'll be able to play this weekend. Daniels said that he's taking things one day at a time.

"I feel good, feel good to be back. Just taking it day by day," Daniels said.

Daniels is wearing a brace on his left arm when he is on the field and he said that it keeps him from being able to fully extend that arm. He added that it does limit him in any way when it comes to throwing or handing off and we'll find out in the near future whether he'll get to show off those skills this weekend.

item.title: Robert Saleh: Derrick Henry still has aura
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: For eight seasons, Derrick Henry helped power the Titans offense, becoming one of the league’s best and most feared running backs in the process.
item.content:encoded:
For eight seasons, Derrick Henry helped power the Titans offense, becoming one of the league’s best and most feared running backs in the process.

He departed Tennessee after the 2023 season, but he’s still been plenty dangerous with Baltimore. He currently leads the NFL with six rushing touchdowns through the first three weeks.

In his first season as Titans head coach, Robert Saleh wasn’t with the club alongside Henry. But he is well aware of the legacy Henry left in the building, and knows Henry will be plenty challenging to slow down as Tennessee takes on Baltimore this weekend.

“First of all, I still think he has aura,” Saleh said in his Wednesday press conference. “The guy's an unbelievable football player destined for the Hall of Fame. Everything you hear about the man, his off the field work habits, how he interacts with people, and then who he is on the field.

“I mean, he's been a very special man in that regard. I've never coached with him, but I've always gotten a chance to see him from afar and go against him. And again, he's an animal. Still running like he's 25 years old. He's a tremendous challenge, and anytime you're trying to replace a Hall of Famer, it's not going to be easy.”

The Titans have Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears carrying the load at running back now.

It will be tough for them to try and match Henry on Sunday, but they’ll have to try.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: Mutual respect with Maxx Crosby brings out the best in both of us
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "He's one of the best competitors in the league," Mahomes said of Crosby.
item.content:encoded:
Not many quarterbacks look forward to seeing Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby on the other side of the line of scrimmage, but Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes says he does look forward to the intense competition he gets when Crosby is on the field.

Mahomes said that with the Raiders on the schedule for Sunday, he's extra motivated to play his best, because he knows Crosby is going to bring his best.

"He's one of the best competitors in the league," Mahomes said of Crosby. "That's where the respect comes from, we have that mutual want to be the best on the field when we're out there. You go against those guys, it brings out the best in you. There's a ton of respect for how he plays the game of football, how he competes and the man he is. When I step on that football field I'm going to need my best because he's going to bring his best, and that's when you get the best games out there."

Mahomes said he considers Crosby a friend and that the two of them texted each other during the offseason to encourage each other as they were both recovering from knee injuries. And Mahomes is looking forward to beating his friend on Sunday.

"It's what pure football is, when the best competitors compete against each other," Mahomes said. "At the end of the day, you want the great competitors, the great players in this league because it makes the league better. And it makes it, when you go out there and do get the win, even better."

item.title: There's "a chance" Joey Porter Jr. will play for the Cowboys on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Although few were willing to call it what it was, it's obvious that former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hadn't played in Week 1, Week 2, or Week 3 for the Steelers because he hadn't gotten a new contract.
item.content:encoded:
Although few were willing to call it what it was, it's obvious that former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hadn't played in Week 1, Week 2, or Week 3 for the Steelers because he hadn't gotten a new contract.

With the Steelers already ruling Porter out for Thursday night's Week 4 game at Cleveland, it's possible the Cowboys will rule him in for Sunday at Houston.

Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, there is "a chance" Porter will play on Sunday. Said Clarence Hill Jr. of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram not long after the news of the trade broke, Porter will play on Sunday "as long as the back feels good."

With Porter apparently accepting that the trade to the Cowboys won't include a new contract, there's no reason to use the back as an excuse to not play. If/when he does play, it will confirm that the entire back/conditioning thing was all about getting a new contract from the Steelers.

Not that confirmation is needed. It's obvious that his training-camp hold-in had extended into the regular season. The Steelers opted to take the path of least resistance. The Cowboys likely won't have to come up with a strategy to get Porter to suit up and play.

From Porter's perspective, that's fine. There's a flaw in the Collective Bargaining Agreement that works to the benefit of the players. Given that the CBA is loaded up with so many team-friendly terms, why shouldn't the players use anything they can to get what they want?

item.title: Sean McVay says NFL told him pass interference should not have been called on Josh Wallace
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The call negated what appeared to be a game-sealing interception for the Rams and set up the Broncos' game-winning touchdown.
item.content:encoded:
The game-changing pass interference call on Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was a bad call, according to Rams head coach Sean McVay.

McVay said today that the league office told him pass interference should not have been called on Wallace.

The penalty was huge, as it negated what would have been Wallace's interception with 1:09 remaining in the game and the Rams leading 26-23. Instead of the Rams getting the ball back and almost certainly winning, the penalty gave the Broncos first-and-goal, setting up a touchdown and a 30-26 Broncos win.

Wallace did make contact with Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant, although it was the kind of contact that frequently goes un-called, and Bryant also made contact with Wallace and could have been flagged for offensive pass interference. Bryant acknowledged that he flopped to sell the call.

The controversial call was one of the biggest penalties of this NFL season. And, according to McVay, the NFL now says it was a flag that should not have been thrown.

item.title: Dan Campbell: Jared Goff is tough, durable, resilient, which you have to be at QB
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Through three weeks, there have been several injuries to starting quarterbacks around the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Through three weeks, there have been several injuries to starting quarterbacks around the NFL.

That isn’t something the Lions have had to deal with over the last several years with Jared Goff, who has not missed a start since 2021.

Head coach Dan Campbell appreciates that about his veteran starter.

“He’s durable, he’s tough, he's resistant, resilient. And he's been that way. He's really been that way his whole career,” Campbell said in his Wednesday press conferences via transcript from the team. “And I know there have been some of these and doesn't mean that things won't come up, but there is. And look, he plays through things too now. That's the other thing, and I guess that plays into the toughness.

“There are things that he gets that people don't even know about that he goes out there and plays and he's good. But I mean, during the week, it's not like he feels good. But he doesn't complain about it. He doesn't miss practice. He's going to be out there because he's our captain, he's our leader. And he knows that for him, it's an accountability thing. 'Well, if I say that something hurts a little bit and I don't go out there to practice, well then I can't say anything to the next guy that’s got a little bump and bruise.' So, it says a lot, it means a lot. And you've got to be tough at that position. And our guy is, it says a ton.”

Goff is off to a good start in 2026, having completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards with eight touchdowns and no interceptions in the first three games.

The Lions will face the Panthers on Sunday Night Football this weekend.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets filled an open spot on their 53-man roster on Thursday morning.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets filled an open spot on their 53-man roster on Thursday morning.

They announced that they have signed offensive lineman Kohl Levao off of their practice squad. They also signed cornerback Jordan Clark and kicker Blake Grupe to the practice squad after waiving them off the active roster earlier this week.

Levao spent the last two seasons on the Jets' practice squad and did not appear in any regular season action. He's also played in the UFL since leaving Hawaii after the 2022 season.

The Jets are set to be without left guard Dylan Parham this week with a knee injury, so Levao gives them more depth heading into Sunday's road game against the Bears.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes: Raiders' 3-0 record is for real, expecting a hostile environment Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas has been a friendly place for the Chiefs to play since it opened in 2020.
item.content:encoded:
Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas has been a friendly place for the Chiefs to play since it opened in 2020.

The Chiefs have played seven games in the building and they've won six of them, including Super Bowl LVIII. That win came over the 49ers, but the other six games have been against the Raiders and the only Chiefs loss came as both teams played out the string in Week 18 of the 2025 season.

Patrick Mahomes did not play in that game, so he's never lost to the Raiders in their current home and he's used to playing in front of Chiefs-leaning crowds when he has been in Vegas in the past. With the Raiders riding a 3-0 start into Sunday's game, the expectation is that things will be a bit more balanced and Mahomes said that he's preparing for less hospitality than he's experienced in the past.

"I love playing football. It doesn’t matter to me," Mahomes said. "I love the Chiefs fans traveling, it’s always cool to see the red in the stadium and hear “Home of the Chiefs” in the national anthem, but, at the end of the day, it’s about playing football. I wouldn’t be surprised if it’s a very hostile environment, trying to take it back to those Oakland Raiders days. I’m excited just for the challenge, you know? They’ve playing great football, you can see it on tape. That 3-0 record’s real. They’ve been playing great the entire season and, for us, it’s another step, another challenge we have to go up there and match."

The Chiefs are 3-0 as well, which makes Sunday's matchup a marquee game in Week 4 and one that could have long-reaching ramifications on the AFC West race.

item.title: Matthew Stafford close to becoming the first QB with 150 touchdowns on two teams
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is closing in on a unique achievement in NFL history.
item.content:encoded:
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is closing in on a unique achievement in NFL history.

Stafford has 147 touchdown passes since he was traded to the Rams in 2021, and if he throws three more, he'll be the first player in NFL history with 150 or more touchdown passes on two different teams.

In his 12 years with the Lions, Stafford threw 282 touchdown passes.

Stafford is sixth in NFL history with 429 career touchdown passes. Only Tom Brady, Drew Brees, Peyton Manning, Aaron Rodgers and Brett Favre are ahead of him.

item.title: The Bengals are the only AFC team Trevor Lawrence has never beaten
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has faced the Bengals three times in his NFL career and none of those contests has ended with a Jacksonville victory.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has faced the Bengals three times in his NFL career and none of those contests has ended with a Jacksonville victory.

The Bengals won at home by a field goal in Lawrence's rookie season in a game best remembered as the one that was followed by then-coach Urban Meyer staying behind to have a little fun at a local bar rather than travel home with his team. The Bengals won in overtime behind Jake Browning in 2023 and Browning came in to rally them to a win again after Joe Burrow was injured late in last season's game in Cincinnati.

Those results make the Bengals the only AFC team that Lawrence has not beaten since he entered the league as the first overall pick in 2021 and he acknowledged that's something he's aware of during a Wednesday press conference.

“We gotta make it turn. We gotta go win it," Lawrence said. "It’s definitely something that, when you’re going into the game, you think about. You’re not sitting there thinking about it every second of the day and all week, but I’ve thought about it. It’s a team that we haven’t beat. We lost a tough one there early in the season last year and that's one that we definitely we want back. All those things you think about and you move on. You have to put your energy toward something that actually does something for you, which is preparing and getting ready to go."

Both teams are 2-1 heading into Sunday's game, so it's an opportunity for the Jags to get an early leg up in the AFC playoff race in addition to getting Lawrence a clean sweep of the conference.

item.title: Cowboys could face a franchise-tag dilemma between George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Joey Porter Jr. trade could eventually work to the benefit of George Pickens.
item.content:encoded:
The Joey Porter Jr. trade could eventually work to the benefit of George Pickens. Or, thanks to Pickens, to the advantage of Porter.

The Cowboys tagged Pickens in 2026, at a franchise tender of $27.298 million. With the market at the position now north of $42 million, that's a great bargain for Dallas. It's so good that they could tag him again in 2027, at $32.758 million.

They also could tag cornerback Joey Porter Jr., at a number that will be far below the top of the market at the position.

But here's the catch. They can't tag both. Every team has one — and only one — to use per year.

For the Cowboys, that means choosing one or the other. Which will create potentially compelling negotiations, with the Cowboys possibly working hard to get one signed so that the other can be tagged.

For the players, who are allowed to collude, one potential strategy would be to take the position that they won't negotiate until the tag deadline comes and goes. That will likely result in one being tagged, and the other having a straight shot at the open market.

Complicating the situation is the fact that both players are represented by David Mulugheta of Athletes First.

It gives the players an element of power over the situation. They can prevent the Cowboys from keeping both or, at a minimum, they can force the Cowboys to compete with other interested teams as to one of them.

Presumably, the Cowboys have a plan. (Then again, they didn't have a plan with seven seconds left against the Ravens.) It could be as simple as using the inevitability of one of them becoming a free agent to get the most out of both of them. Then, after the season, they'll decide which one to tag.

And if/when one of them leaves, they'll be in line for a third-round compensatory pick in 2028. Which will either replace the third-round pick they sent to Pittsburgh for Pickens, or offset the 2028 second-round pick that they'll be giving up for Porter.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Porter will miss his fourth straight game.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appeared to be making progress toward a return to the Steelers lineup this week, but any hope he would make his 2026 debut on Thursday night against the Browns has been dashed.

Porter was ruled out by the Steelers on Wednesday. Porter was listed as a full participant in practice on Monday and Tuesday with conditioning work given as the only reason why he was on the list. He was limited on Wednesday, however, and the back injury that kept him on the physically unable to perform list all summer is back on the report as well.

While the back injury and need for conditioning are the health reasons for Porter's absence, his inability to secure a contract extension has been the backdrop to the weekly questions about his availability and the one step forward, one step back nature of his practice work does little to suggest that the contract isn't playing a role.

The Steelers have other injury concerns at corner. Jalen Ramsey is listed as questionable with what he said is a broken wrist and Brandin Echols has the same designation due to a concussion.

Running back Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out for the second straight game.

It looks like wide receiver Puka Nacua will be back in the Rams' lineup this week.

item.title: Report: No new contract for Joey Porter Jr. in Dallas (at least for now)
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wanted a new contract.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wanted a new contract. He didn't get one. He wanted a trade. He got one.

So now he'll get a new contract, right?

Wrong, perhaps.

Via Clarence Hill Jr. of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, the trade of Porter from the Steelers to the Cowboys comes without a new contract.

The Cowboys inherit the $3.052 million balance of his $3.924 million base salary for 2026. They also acquire the ability to apply the franchise tag to Porter in 2027.

With the 2026 franchise tag for cornerbacks at $21.161 million and the market well above $30 million, the Cowboys could be tempted to tag Porter and kick the can.

They also could let him leave, harvest a third-round compensatory pick in 2028, and thereby offset the second-round pick they'll be sending to the Steelers that year (and the 2027 sixth-rounder).

For both sides, the move smacked of desperation. The Cowboys are desperate to improve their defense. And the Steelers were desperate to get out of a contract impasse that had no middle ground.

item.title: Wink Martindale offers to help "outclassed" Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Coaching inexperience is holding the Cowboys back.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' failure to beat the Ravens in Rio came from all three phases of the team. The offense failed to turn first and goal from the two with 20 seconds left into a game-winning touchdown, the special teams served up favorable field position on the kickoff after the game-tying field goal, and the defense allowed the Ravens to gain enough yards to set up the game-winning field goal.

The ultimate blame resides with coach Brian Schottenheimer, who shouldn't be learning the job of being an effective head coach while on the job.

Still, the defense continues to be a problem. Long-time NFL and college defensive coach Wink Martindale spoke bluntly about the situation during his latest appearance on Talkin' Ball with Pat Leonard.

"I don't want to be an asshole but he’s being outclassed right now," Martindale said regarding Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker. "So Jerry [Jones] can call me and I'll go help him. But, you know, I'm talking about helping the coordinator."

Matching a head coach who is learning the job on the fly with a defensive coordinator who is learning the job on the fly isn't ideal. It would have been useful for Schottenheimer, who has no former NFL head coaches on his staff, to have access to a key lieutenant who has done the job of head coach before — and whose experiences can help Schottenheimer realize the right answers to the test before he turns the paperwork in.

That's really the problem with the Cowboys. They lack the ability to prepare for the unique situations that experienced coaches know how to address. It played out on Sunday, giving the Cowboys a loss that could echo into January

And that could be the difference between making it to the playoffs or going home after Week 18, for the third straight season.

item.title: Report: Brian Burns tore his meniscus in addition to his ACL
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants linebacker Brian Burns is set to have knee surgery on Thursday and doctors will reportedly be repairing more than just his ACL.
item.content:encoded:
Giants linebacker Brian Burns is set to have knee surgery on Thursday and doctors will reportedly be repairing more than just his ACL.

Dan Duggan of TheAthletic.com reports that Burns also tore the meniscus in his right knee when he was injured in last Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. Both injuries will be addressed during his surgery in New York.

Burns's teammate Malik Nabers suffered the same two injuries in late September last year. The wide receiver was able to return for the start of this season, but has had a quiet start with 12 catches for 96 yards through three weeks.

The Giants will be hoping Burns can follow Nabers's path and be ready for the start of next season. They'd surely prefer his return come with the impact he's provided in the past, but the first step will be getting healthy enough to play.

item.title: Cowboys send Steelers 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr.
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: One of the NFL's best young cornerbacks is heading to Dallas, and Pittsburgh is getting two picks.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys are sending the Steelers two draft picks in the trade that brings cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas.

The Steelers will get a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick, according to multiple reports. The 2027 sixth-round pick is the Steelers' own sixth-rounder, which they had previously traded to the Cowboys as part of the George Pickens deal.

For the Cowboys, it's a move that's about bolstering the defense immediately with a player who's in the final year of his contract, whereas for the Steelers it's about acquiring future draft capital for a player who clearly wanted more money than the Steelers were going to be willing to pay.

Whether the Cowboys pay that money remains to be seen. It would be unusual to trade for a player in the last year of his contract and not give him an extension, but the Cowboys could also be thinking that they'll get the rest of this season out of Porter and then evaluate whether to sign him to a long-term deal or let him walk in free agency.

The Cowboys could be calculating that getting one good season out of Porter this year and then letting him leave for a lucrative contract with another team wouldn't be the worst thing, as that would likely bring them a third-round compensatory pick in 2028. Essentially, they'd be renting Porter for one season and only paying him the $3.924 million salary on the final year of his contract, at the price of moving down from the second to the third round in 2028.

For the Steelers, they're losing one of their most talented players, but it had become clear that things weren't going to work out for Porter in Pittsburgh. He was unhappy with his contract and still hasn't played this season, officially because of a back injury — a back injury that the Steelers may have calculated was not going to heal until they gave him the contract he wanted.

Whether Porter gets that contract in Dallas this year, in Dallas next offseason, or with some other team next offseason, he's now a Cowboy, and the Steelers have acquired two draft picks for a player who wanted out.

item.title: Bears open 21-day practice window for Kyler Gordon
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon may finally be close to a return.
item.content:encoded:
Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon may finally be close to a return.

The Bears have officially opened Gordon's 21-day practice window, which means they have three weeks to activate him from the physically unable to perform list.

Although the Bears had only a walk-through practice on Wednesday, they estimated that he would have been healthy enough to fully participate if Wednesday had been a full practice.

That's good news for a player who has been notable mostly for his absence, and for the Bears' odd reluctance to say when — or if — he will be healthy enough to play. Gordon didn't practice at all in training camp, didn't play at all in the preseason, and is out at least the first four games of the regular season as part of his PUP designation.

It's not a sure thing that Gordon will be activated off PUP, but opening the practice window at least raises that possibility.

The Bears signed Gordon to a three-year, $40 million contract extension last year, and Gordon played in just three games last season as he struggled with groin, hamstring and calf injuries. His calf is the apparent reason he hasn't been able to do anything this year, and it will be the most-watched calf in Chicago until he either returns within the next three weeks, or is officially declared out for the season.

item.title: Drake Maye: I love playing for Mike Vrabel, that's not going to change
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day.

While Vrabel said he didn't "have much to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source," Maye's response avoided discussion of where the report came from and focused on how much he likes playing for the coach.

"Coach Vrabel’s been one of the best football coaches I’ve had in my life," Maye said, via a transcript from the team. "I think Coach Vrabel’s been one of the biggest things as to why this has been so enjoyable for me is playing for Coach. I think we all feel that way in the locker room. He pushes us hard. I’ve loved playing for him, and it’s not going to change. It hasn’t changed, and it won’t change. The way he pushes me, and he coaches the quarterbacks in a way that I really respect, and I’m looking forward to getting going, proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football."

Maye also fielded questions about whether an injury to his shoulder is contributing to his poor play so far this season and there will continue to be questions about what's bothering a player who finished second in MVP voting last year until he starts playing at that level again.

item.title: Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Contract impasse ends with Porter being sent to a new team.
item.content:encoded:
Last year, once the Cowboys realized that linebacker Micah Parsons wasn't going to play without a new contract, Dallas traded him.

This year, the Steelers apparently have realized that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wouldn't be playing without a new contract. And so they're trading him.

Per multiple reports, the Steelers are sending Porter to the Cowboys.

The full terms have yet to emerge. The separate question will be whether the Cowboys will give Porter the contract he couldn't get in Pittsburgh.

Dallas could decide to ride it out in 2026, with Porter making $3.924 million. Then, they could apply the franchise tag in 2027.

It's hard to imagine the Cowboys tradining for a player who apparently doesn't intend to play until he gets a new deal.

The common link between Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, and Parsons is that both are represented by David Mulugheta of Athletes First. Mulugheta also represents receiver George Pickens, who was traded by the Steelers to the Cowboys in May 2025.

The Cowboys haven't given Pickens a new deal. For 2026, they tagged him. For receivers, the franchise tender is well below market value. It is for cornerbacks, too.

Much will be revealed in the coming hours. For now, the most important point is that the impasse between the Steelers and Porter has ended with Porter being sent to a new team.
